sc_01.rationale: Bilateral intracranial leads and an implanted neurostimulator.

sc_02.rationale: The system senses LFPs and adjusts stimulation amplitude in closed loop.

sc_03.rationale: Authorized adjunctive Parkinson disease therapy programming option.

sc_04.rationale: Local field potentials are direct neural signals; thresholds and control outputs are derived.

sc_05.rationale: Deterministic threshold control adapts stimulation amplitude.

sc_06.rationale: Long-term implanted system and longitudinal therapy.

sc_07.rationale: Adaptive mode is operationally reversible, but implantation and removal are clinically burdensome.

sc_08.rationale: Clinician defines limits; controller acts automatically; patient can pause.

sc_09.rationale: Prescription clinical programming with operation outside clinic after setup.

sc_10.rationale: Labeled Parkinson disease population includes adults with disability and many older patients.

sc_11.rationale: FDA approved in 2025 and subsequent supplements/recalls exist.

sc_12.rationale: Programmer communications, proprietary updates and essential implanted support create dependency and security exposure.

intended_uses: U.S. prescription adaptive DBS programming option for the exact labeled Parkinson disease indication using compatible Percept systems and trained practitioners.
Authorization-specific public-evidence assessment and residual evidence acquisition.
excluded_uses: More than one implanted neurostimulator for adaptive use.
Other diseases, neural targets, biomarkers, devices, algorithms or jurisdictions.
Autonomous diagnosis or control outside clinician-defined bounds.
Claims of superiority over continuous DBS.
Coercive, surveillance, enhancement, workplace, education, justice, defence or consumer use.
populations: Adults with levodopa-responsive Parkinson disease of at least four years duration, not adequately controlled with medication, within the existing FDA indication.
ADAPT-PD evidence population: carefully selected existing Percept PC users with stable cDBS response and usable alpha-beta LFP signal.
contexts: Research evidence from 10 sites in the United States, Canada, Netherlands and France

legacy_bounded_decision.strongest_supported_claim: FDA P960009/S478 authorizes an optional adaptive DBS programming feature for the exact labeled Parkinson disease indication. In carefully screened existing cDBS responders using a single compatible Percept neurostimulator, ADAPT-PD supports that single- and dual-threshold alpha-beta LFP control can maintain good on-time within a post-hoc two-hour-per-day margin for many evaluable participants, with clinician-defined limits, patient pause to cDBS and substantial setup/monitoring requirements. The evidence does not establish superiority to cDBS or complete CL-4 conformance for current deployments.

Autonomous diagnosis, target selection or stimulation outside clinician-defined bounds.
Clinically meaningful battery-life benefit from TEED reduction.
Absence of adverse events, cybersecurity risk, communication failure or supplier dependency.

jurisdictional_conflicts: The decision is bounded to the U.S. PMA authorization. Research sites in Canada, Netherlands and France do not establish marketing authorization in those jurisdictions.

Incorrect sensing or response in unapproved multiple-INS configurations.
Communication, software-update and proprietary supplier dependency.
Selected-cohort and post-hoc-endpoint limitations may inflate broad interpretations.
